title: Scalene Yang-Baxter triples realize all nearest-neighbour Hamiltonians with global additive symmetries
authors: Pramod Padmanabhan, Somnath Maity, Akash Sinha, Vladimir Korepin
abstract: We establish that bond Hamiltonian densities, up to local difference terms whose sum vanishes under periodic boundary conditions, lying in the commutant of bond operators, $w_j\pm w_{j+1}$, is a necessary and sufficient condition for a one-dimensional nearest-neighbour Hamiltonian to conserve a uniform or staggered sum of the one-site operators $w_j$. Starting from these local commutants, we show that every such Hamiltonian and its conserved charge can be obtained from monodromy matrices constructed using regular and non-regular members of scalene Yang-Baxter triples. The results hold on periodic chains of length $L\geq3$, with even length required in the staggered case. The results do not require translation invariance, and hence the interaction on each bond can be chosen independently from the full corresponding commutant. Our representation-independent construction applies in arbitrary finite local dimension and exhausts the Hamiltonians with either prescribed additive symmetry, without requiring ordinary Yang-Baxter integrability. We illustrate the construction with spin-$\tfrac12$ and spin-1 systems and discuss its relation to the double-commutant theorem. Classifying the one-site generators $w$ and their associated bond commutants provides a route to classifying such Hamiltonians with additive conserved charges.
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive classification scheme for one-dimensional nearest-neighbor Hamiltonians that possess global additive symmetries. It establishes that these Hamiltonians are characterized by their bond densities commuting with the symmetry generators, which are systematically constructed using scalene Yang-Baxter triples. This method is powerful because it does not require the full translation invariance or standard Yang-Baxter integrability.
main_problem: To develop a systematic method for constructing one-dimensional nearest-neighbor Hamiltonians that possess global additive symmetries (uniform or staggered sums of local operators).
main_result: Every such Hamiltonian can be constructed from monodromy matrices built using regular and non-regular members of scalene Yang-Baxter triples, providing a classification beyond standard integrability assumptions.
method: The construction relies on establishing a necessary and sufficient condition: the Hamiltonian density must lie in the commutant of the bond operators, which is then realized using the algebraic structure provided by the scalene Yang-Baxter equation.
model_or_system: The study focuses on one-dimensional quantum spin chains on closed lattices of length L, characterized by nearest-neighbor Hamiltonians and associated conserved charges ($Q_+$ and $Q_-$).
key_observables: The conserved charges ($Q_+$ and $Q_-$) and the structure of the bond Hamiltonian densities ($h_{j,j+1}$).
important_parameters: The lattice length L (with specific requirements for staggered symmetry), and the local dimension of the spin system (e.g., spin-1/2, spin-1).
main_assumptions: The results hold modulo local difference terms whose sum vanishes under periodic boundary conditions, and the method is representation-independent.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the local commutant condition for conservation laws, then shows that the scalene Yang-Baxter equation provides the algebraic framework to realize these symmetries via monodromy matrices, culminating in a classification of the resulting Hamiltonians.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, generalized algebraic framework (scalene YBE) to classify integrable or quasi-integrable models, extending beyond the constraints of standard Yang-Baxter integrability, which is crucial for understanding complex many-body dynamics.
